description: A benchmark corpus of 8 sentences rendered in 18 language/register variants for tokenization analysis. CAVEATS: Several non-English entries are public-domain script samples rather than literal translations of the English source sentence. In particular: (1) some Classical Chinese, Tibetan, Khmer, Amharic, Inuktitut, and Cherokee entries are well-known proverbs, UDHR phrases, or common phrasebook expressions in the target script — chosen to faithfully sample the script's tokenization characteristics, not for translation fidelity; (2) legalese and Victorian-prose register variants are original renderings of the meaning, not translations. The metric under study is tokenization behaviour of each script/language pair, not semantic equivalence.

languages.name: English
languages.notes: Baseline; cl100k_base and o200k_base were trained primarily on English text

languages.name: Classical Chinese (wenyan)
languages.notes: Expected champion for token efficiency — dense Han ideographs map to very few BPE tokens per character

languages.name: Modern Chinese (Mandarin)
languages.notes: Contrast with Classical Chinese; more characters per concept than wenyan

languages.name: Burmese
languages.notes: Non-Latin script, low-resource in BPE vocabulary — expected high tokens/char ratio

languages.name: Tibetan
languages.notes: Non-Latin abugida with complex stacking characters; very underrepresented in GPT vocabularies

languages.name: Khmer
languages.notes: Non-Latin script with dense consonant clusters; expected poor tokenization compression

languages.name: Amharic
languages.notes: Ge'ez abugida; each glyph encodes consonant+vowel — interesting byte-to-token ratio

languages.name: Telugu
languages.notes: Agglutinative Dravidian; long compound words expected to fragment heavily under BPE

languages.name: Tamil
languages.notes: Agglutinative Dravidian; classical literary tradition with separate script from Telugu

languages.name: Malayalam
languages.notes: Agglutinative Dravidian; script has the most glyphs of any Indic script — high byte cost

languages.name: Sinhala
languages.notes: Abugida spoken in Sri Lanka; very low BPE vocabulary coverage expected

languages.name: Georgian
languages.notes: Agglutinative; unique script (Mkhedruli) with no Latin cognates — clean script-effect signal

languages.name: Inuktitut (Unified Canadian Aboriginal Syllabics)
languages.notes: Polysynthetic language; entire clauses can be one word — extreme agglutination test

languages.name: Cherokee
languages.notes: Syllabary invented by Sequoyah; unique Unicode block, near-zero BPE coverage expected

languages.name: Finnish
languages.notes: Agglutinative but Latin-script control; isolates agglutination cost from script exoticism

languages.name: Turkish
languages.notes: Agglutinative Latin-script control; regular vowel harmony produces long but predictable words

languages.name: Legalese
languages.notes: English register variant; low-frequency vocabulary expected to stress the tokenizer

languages.name: Victorian prose
languages.notes: English register variant; archaic vocabulary and long nominal phrases for contrast

translations.my: မင်္ဂလာပါ၊ ကမ္ဘာလောက။
translations.km: សួស្តី ពិភពលោក។
translations.en-legalese: Greetings are hereby extended to the world at large.
translations.en-victorian: Salutations, thou boundless and magnificent world.

sentences.english: The cat sat on the mat.

translations.en: The cat sat on the mat.
translations.my: ကြောင်သည် ကြမ်းဖျာပေါ်တွင် ထိုင်သည်။
translations.km: ឆ្មានោះអង្គុយនៅលើកំណាត់ព្រំ។
translations.en-legalese: The aforementioned feline party did occupy and remain seated upon the textile floor covering hereinafter referred to as the mat.
translations.en-victorian: The cat, a most contemplative creature of domestic habit, had reposed itself upon the mat with serene and unhurried composure.

translations.my: အသိပညာသည် အာဏာဖြစ်သည်။
translations.km: ចំណេះដឹងគឺជាអំណាច។
translations.en-legalese: Herein it is affirmed that the possession and application of knowledge constitutes, in law and in fact, a form of power.
translations.en-victorian: It has long been held as an incontrovertible maxim that the acquisition of knowledge doth confer upon its possessor a power most formidable.

sentences.english: I would like a cup of tea, please.

translations.en: I would like a cup of tea, please.
translations.my: ကျေးဇူးပြု၍ လက်ဖက်ရည်တစ်ခွက် ပေးပါ။
translations.km: សូមអោយខ្ញុំមួយពែងតែផង។
translations.te: దయచేసి నాకు ఒక కప్పు టీ ఇవ్వండి.
translations.si: කරුණාකර මට එක් කෝප්පයක් තේ දෙන්න.
translations.tr: Lütfen bir fincan çay alabilir miyim?
translations.en-legalese: The undersigned hereby requests that one (1) unit of brewed tea be provided forthwith, subject to available supply.
translations.en-victorian: If it should not prove too great an imposition, I should be most grateful to receive a cup of tea at your earliest convenience.

sentences.english: The early bird catches the worm.

translations.en: The early bird catches the worm.
translations.my: စောစောထ ငှက်သည် ကောင်မွှားကို ဖမ်းနိုင်သည်။
translations.km: បក្សីដែលក្រោកពីព្រលឹមទើបចាប់បានដង្ករ។
translations.si: උදේ ඉක්මනට නැඟිටින කුරුල්ලා පණු අල්ලයි.
translations.en-legalese: That party who initiates activity at an early hour shall be entitled to the first and primary claim upon available resources, including but not limited to worms.
translations.en-victorian: It is the industrious and earliest-rising bird which, by virtue of its admirable punctuality, secures for itself the coveted worm.

translations.my: အချိန်သည် မြှားကဲ့သို့ ပျံသန်းသည်။
translations.km: ពេលវេលាហោះដូចស្រួចព្រួញ។
translations.en-legalese: Time, for the purposes of this instrument, shall be deemed to elapse at a rate comparable to that of a projectile, specifically an arrow, in flight.
translations.en-victorian: How swift and merciless is the passage of time, which moves with all the swiftness and precision of an arrow loosed from the archer's bow.

sentences.english: All that glitters is not gold.

translations.en: All that glitters is not gold.
translations.zh-modern: 闪闪发光的未必是黄金。
translations.my: တောက်ပသောအရာ အားလုံးသည် ရွှေမဟုတ်ပေ။
translations.km: អ្វីដែលផ្លេកផ្លេកមិនមែនជាមាស ទាំងអស់ទេ។
translations.ka: ყველაფერი, რაც ბრწყინავს, ოქრო არ არის.
translations.fi: Kaikki se ei ole kultaa, mikä kiiltää.
translations.en-legalese: Notwithstanding any superficial luminosity, no warranty, express or implied, is made that any substance or matter so gleaming constitutes gold or any gold equivalent.
translations.en-victorian: One must not be so readily deceived by outward brilliance, for it hath long been observed that not all which glitters with such enticing lustre is, in truth, wrought of gold.

sentences.english: May you live in interesting times.

translations.en: May you live in interesting times.
translations.zh-modern: 愿你生活在有趣的时代。
translations.my: သင်သည် စိတ်ဝင်စားဖွယ် ကာလတွင် နေထိုင်ပါစေ။
translations.km: សូមឲ្យអ្នករស់នៅក្នុងសម័យដ៏គួរចាប់អារម្មណ៍។
translations.en-legalese: It is hereby wished upon the addressee that the period of their natural life shall coincide with times of notable and material interest, as determined by reasonable standards.
translations.en-victorian: It is my most sincere and heartfelt wish that your days upon this earth shall be spent amid times of the most extraordinary and uncommon interest.
